title: Police held at bay in standoff
article: A four-hour standoff ended peacefully Tuesday after a man armed with a pistol and rifle threatened to kill himself or police officers and barricaded himself in a house on Con. 3
Details were sketchy, but reports indicated the man was arrested about 10:30 p.m.
The incident, which began at about 6:30 p.m., occurred in what is normally a quiet country neighbourhood.
Police were called to the home and immediately blocked off Con. 3 as they moved in to surround the house, which is located just south of the County Road 20, formerly Highway 18.
At one point while police were approaching the house, the man fired a handgun inside and threatened to commit suicide or shoot police.
A Windsor police hostage negotiator and members of Windsor's emergency services unit were called in to assist in the standoff.
It is the town's second such incident in a month.
On Oct. 30, Robert Scott Carpenter was shot to death after police officers were attacked with a knife while responding to a domestic violence call.
Tuesday's incident occurred just a few kilometres from the scene of an earlier shooting.

A steady stream of residents were turned away at the road block. A police officer was able to speak to the man by telephone for most of the stand off as members of the Windsor Police tactical squad positioned themselves outside the house for a long wait.
Tensions rose when the man, carrying a shotgun, walked into the back yard close to the officers lying under cover in the bush. But he returned to the house without firing.
Amherstburg police officers were the first to arrive and they kept the house under observation until the Windsor police negotiator arrived at about 9 p.m. to speak to the armed man.
There was an ambulance standing by on County Road 20 throughout the incident.

Police believe there was a woman in the house, but she was able to leave the home. The armed man asked the police negotiator about her well being. He was told she was speaking to police officers but she was fine.
There were reports that the man trashed the home and tried to rip the phone from the wall, but police were able to maintain contact.
Last Thursday an Amherstburg police officer was cleared of any wrongdoing in the shooting death of Carpenter, 36.
The Oct. 30 incident began as a domestic dispute between Carpenter and his common-law wife.
Lisa Stewart desperately implored police to get her two children out of their home, where Carpenter was brandishing a knife.
An officer's pleas for Carpenter to open the locked door fell on deaf ears and a brief standoff ensued.

When the two other officers arrived as backup they assisted their comrade on the porch. When the front door suddenly opened, one of the officers fell onto the foyer floor and was set upon by Carpenter wielding a knife in his right hand.
The officer suffered wounds to his head and chest and a uniformed officer pulled his pistol and ordered Carpenter to drop the knife. But he continued to slash at the downed officer.
Another officer fired a shot to protect his colleague and it struck Carpenter in the leg. He died three hours later.
Two officers suffered minor injuries.
